comparison: Both evaluate stimulus-selective neurons (C41-C44, C72) and find them SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes statistical significance (p=0.011) and consistency with animal literature. Peer reviewers confirm the neural data analysis is sound and acknowledge convincing evidence for stimulus-correlated activity. Complete agreement on this finding.

Both address the main conclusion about subcortical involvement in consciousness (C6, C56-C61, C82-C83). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with appropriate caveats about sample size. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, acknowledging the study is 'important' and 'valuable' but expressing concerns about motor confounds, small sample size, and generalizability that prevent full endorsement of the strong conclusion.

Both evaluate the mechanistic interpretation about STN function and decision thresholds (C62-C68). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting the hypothesis is plausible but speculative with limited computational modeling. Peer reviewers also rate UNCERTAIN, with no explicit validation of the mechanism and concerns about small sample size undermining mechanistic interpretations. Agreement on uncertainty.

Both evaluate cue-selective and task-selective neurons (C33-C40). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with appropriate statistics and notes motor independence from delayed response design. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, with editor stating 'convincing evidence' and reviewers praising statistical rigor. Minor difference: peer R3 also includes C69-C70 about pre-stimulus neurons. Strong agreement.

Both evaluate perception-selective neurons (C45-C52). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, noting statistical significance (p=0.0060) and appropriate controls, with caution about small sample. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, acknowledging 'convincing evidence' but raising significant concerns about the small number of neurons (~8), potential motor confounds, and generalizability. Disagreement on confidence level due to sample size concerns.

Both address timing of neural activity and EEG contextualization (C74-C80). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, praising appropriate acknowledgment of uncertainty about consciousness vs. attention. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 1 explicitly noting the ~150ms timing and no challenges to the bimodal distribution. Agreement on timing findings and appropriate caution.

Both evaluate behavioral quality control and task design (C25-C30 overlap). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED for rigorous behavioral controls. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, praising calibration and stimulus intensity controls, though Reviewer 2 raises concern about verbal responses involving facial muscles (C23). Mostly agreement with one caveat about motor confounds.

Both address study limitations (C73, C81). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, commending self-critical assessment of small sample size and recommendations for future controls. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, explicitly echoing concerns about small neuron numbers and inability to fully exclude motor/post-perceptual confounds. Complete agreement on limitations.

Both address beta oscillation findings (C55). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, appropriately reporting the negative finding but noting sample size limitations. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 suggesting additional LFP analysis could strengthen conclusions, implying the beta-band analysis may be insufficient. Mild disagreement on adequacy of this analysis.

Both evaluate methodological details and recording procedures (C15, C84-C90 overlap). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED for comprehensive methods, technical specifications, and ethical approvals. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, with explicit praise for achieving single-unit recordings and acknowledgment of valuable data contribution. Complete agreement on recording quality.

Both address neuronal isolation and analysis procedures (C3, C31-C32). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED for rigorous quality control and statistical methods. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, acknowledging successful single-unit recordings and valuable contribution. Agreement on data quality, though peer R1 focuses more broadly on recording achievement.

Both evaluate experimental design and delayed response paradigm (C16, C18-C24 overlap). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, noting the delayed response design addresses motor confounds (C22-C23). Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED for behavioral design quality, but Reviewer 2 specifically challenges C23, noting verbal responses involve facial muscle activation. Disagreement on whether motor confounds are fully addressed.

Both address functional heterogeneity (C53-C54). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, noting qualitative observation of little overlap supports functional diversity. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN for the broader perception-selective findings, noting 'interpretations are still very open on these different profiles' given small sample. Peer reviewers less confident about heterogeneity interpretations.

Both address pre-stimulus modulating neurons (C69-C70). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting the task-switching interpretation is speculative. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED for task-related neurons broadly but do not specifically validate the task-switching interpretation for pre-stimulus neurons. Partial overlap with different emphasis.

OpenEval evaluates comprehensive methods including delayed response design (C23: no motor confounds). Peer R10 specifically rates C23 as UNSUPPORTED, with Reviewer 2 noting verbal responses involve facial muscle activation and Reviewer 1 noting inability to fully exclude motor preparatory processing. Direct disagreement on whether motor confounds are adequately controlled.
